definition: A machine translation system developed at the University of Texas and at Siemens which ran on Lisp Machines.
details: A machine translation system developed at the University of Texas and at Siemens which ran on Lisp Machines.

explainer.lead: METAL MT is a machine translation system developed at the University of Texas and at Siemens that ran on Lisp Machines. It is an early example of a machine translation system built for dedicated AI hardware.

tiers.eli5: It is an old translation program that ran on special Lisp computers rather than ordinary PCs. Think of a translator that lived on its own specialized machine.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers encounter METAL MT as historical context for rule-based machine translation on Lisp Machines. The pitfall is treating it as a current tool: it is tied to that hardware and era.
tiers.paperLevel: A machine translation system developed at the University of Texas and at Siemens, running on Lisp Machines. No performance figures or formal specification are given.

explainer.example: A translation task was handled by METAL MT running on a Lisp Machine at the University of Texas or Siemens.
